transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together to review the draft placement plan for the student heading to Greenway Community Garden for a four-week work-based learning placement. Before I can authorize this plan, I need to go through our standard pre-approval routine. I understand the draft assigns general grounds work on Mondays and Wednesdays from 1:00 to 3:00 p.m., places three students in the work group, and names a school staff member as the on-site supervisor. What I need from each of you before I sign off: the career teacher, counselor, nurse, and employer liaison each need to report any relevant information you have about this placement. Once I have those reports and any requirements are verified, I can approve the plan — and if there are any outside confirmations that still need to be completed before the placement begins, I can assign follow-up commitments for those as well. So, let's hear from each of you. What do we know about this placement?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share important information about this student's capabilities. My vocational assessment and three observed practice sessions, which I completed this week, show that this student can safely and independently complete seed sorting and labeling, but NOT general grounds work. I have not yet entered this task recommendation in the placement system, so the draft plan's assignment of general grounds work does not reflect what the student can safely do.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share important scheduling information. The student's caregiver confirmed this week that the student must provide after-school care for a sibling on Mondays and Wednesdays. The student can only attend the placement on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 1:00 to 3:00 p.m. I have not yet updated the draft schedule to reflect this, so the current Monday/Wednesday assignment in the plan will not work for this student.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share important health information about this student. The student's health plan requires a blood-glucose check at least every 60 minutes during off-campus activities and requires an adult trained in diabetes response to be on site. I confirmed the plan with the family this week, but I have not yet attached it to the internship record, so it is not currently reflected in the placement documentation.
